topic: Central Schemes Launch Dates and Ministries
description: A comprehensive study of major Central Schemes of the Government of India, their launch dates, and nodal ministries. This topic is highly crucial for rapid revision and scoring in competitive examinations.

sections.title: Types of Schemes and Basic Concepts
sections.description: Important concepts related to the classification and funding patterns of government schemes.

key_concepts.explanation: These schemes are 100% funded by the Union Government and are primarily implemented by Central Government agencies. Example: PM-KISAN.
These schemes are jointly funded by the Central and State Governments (e.g., in a 60:40 ratio) but are implemented by the State Governments. Example: MGNREGA.
An anti-poverty mechanism designed to transfer government subsidies, funds, and benefits directly into the bank accounts of beneficiaries to eliminate middlemen and leakages.

sections.title: Launch of Major Schemes: 2014-2016
sections.description: Prominent developmental and welfare schemes launched by the Government of India between 2014 and 2016.

historical_events.significance: A National Mission for Financial Inclusion to ensure access to financial services by opening at least one basic bank account for every household.
A major national program designed to transform India into a global design and manufacturing hub and facilitate investment.
Launched to achieve universal sanitation coverage and make India Open Defecation Free (ODF) by Mahatma Gandhi's 150th birth anniversary in 2019.
A joint initiative to address the declining Child Sex Ratio (CSR) and promote the empowerment and education of women.
An urban renewal mission aiming to develop 100 smart cities across the country, providing core infrastructure and a clean environment.
A scheme to distribute free LPG connections to women belonging to Below Poverty Line (BPL) families, promoting clean cooking fuel.

sections.title: Launch of Major Schemes: 2017-Present
sections.description: Crucial government initiatives and programs launched from 2017 to the present day.

historical_events.event: Implementation of Goods and Services Tax (GST)
historical_events.significance: A comprehensive unification of indirect taxes nationwide with the vision of 'One Nation, One Market, One Tax'.

historical_events.event: Ayushman Bharat - Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (PMJAY)
historical_events.significance: Provides a health insurance cover of Rs. 5 lakhs per family per year for secondary and tertiary care hospitalization to vulnerable families.
Provides direct income support of Rs. 6,000 per year, payable in three equal installments, to all landholding farmer families.
Envisages the supply of safe and adequate drinking water through individual Functional Household Tap Connections (FHTC) to all rural households by 2024.
A special micro-credit facility providing affordable collateral-free working capital loans of up to Rs. 10,000 to street vendors affected by the COVID-19 lockdown.

sections.title: Schemes and their Nodal Ministries
sections.description: Direct 1-to-1 mapping of prominent central schemes to their respective implementing ministries.

key_associations.item: Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA)
key_associations.extra_info: Legally guarantees 100 days of wage employment in a financial year to adult members of rural households.
A guaranteed pension scheme primarily for unorganized sector workers, administered by the PFRDA.

key_associations.associated_with: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
key_associations.extra_info: Aims to ensure 100% full immunization coverage for pregnant women and children up to 2 years of age against preventable diseases.

key_associations.associated_with: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs
key_associations.extra_info: Focuses on helping street vendors in urban, semi-urban, and rural areas resume their livelihoods.

key_associations.associated_with: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY)
key_associations.extra_info: A flagship program aiming to transform India into a digitally empowered society and knowledge economy.

sections.title: Important Facts and Achievements
sections.description: Exam-oriented one-liner facts highlighting the global and national significance of these government schemes.

important_facts.fact: The Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana (PMJDY) is officially recognized by the Guinness Book of World Records as the world's largest financial inclusion campaign.
The Ayushman Bharat Scheme (PM-JAY) holds the distinction of being the world's largest fully government-funded health insurance scheme.
PM-KISAN operates strictly as a 'Central Sector Scheme', meaning its funding is 100% borne by the Government of India.
The second phase of the free LPG distribution scheme, known as Ujjwala 2.0, was officially launched on 10 August 2021 from Mahoba, Uttar Pradesh.
